text.headline: NIO Data Leak and Extortion
text.text:
On December 20, criminals were selling a large amount of NIO data on the internet, including 22,800 records of NIO internal employee data, 399,000 records of vehicle owner ID card data, 125,000 records of owner data, 650,000 records of user address data, 4,850,000 records of registered user information, 10,000 records of enterprise and enterprise representative contact data, 490,000 records of orders, 90,000 records of cancellations, 360,000 records of owner relationship data, 170,000 records of owner loan data, and more.

On the afternoon of December 20, NIO's Chief Information Security Scientist and head of the Information Security Committee, Lu Long, published a notice titled "Statement on Data Security Incident" in the NIO official community. On December 11, 2022, NIO received an external email claiming to possess NIO internal data and extorting the equivalent of $2.25 million (approximately 15.705 million RMB at the time) in Bitcoin for the leaked data. Upon receiving the extortion email, the company established a special task force that same day to investigate and respond, and immediately reported the incident to the relevant regulatory authorities. Preliminary investigation revealed that the stolen data consisted of some users' basic information and vehicle sales information from before August 2021.

NIO expressed deep regret for the impact this incident had on users and solemnly committed to bearing responsibility for any losses caused to users by this incident.

media.caption: Full Account Takeover on BMW and Rolls Royce via Misconfigured SSO

text.headline: BMW, Rolls-Royce Supplier SSO Platform Arbitrary User Password Reset Vulnerability
text.text:
The BMW and Rolls-Royce supplier SSO (Single Sign-On) platform is used to access internal tools, development environments, and more. The single sign-on platform's password reset has a vulnerability that allows unauthorized users to reset any user's password. Using the reset password, all functions accessible to the supplier can be accessed, such as obtaining sales documents via VIN (which contain customers' private information).

During fuzzing of the OSS platform, a WADL file was discovered (https://xpita.bmwgroup.com/rest/api/application.wadl) containing a large number of sensitive interfaces. For example, the interface /reset/api/users/example* can retrieve user information based on fuzzed usernames; the /rest/api/chains/accounts/:user_id/totp interface is used to request time-based one-time passwords. This TOTP code is used in password reset, similar to the verification code in two-factor authentication. Testing revealed that after obtaining user information through the user query interface using wildcards, entering the password recovery page to reset the user's password, and obtaining the verification code from /rest/api/chains/accounts/:user_id/totp, submitting it allowed the password reset of the specified user.

media.caption: Remote Code Execution and Access to Hundreds of Internal Tools on Mercedes-Ben via Misconfigured SSO

text.headline: Remote Code Execution via Misconfigured Mercedes-Benz SSO, Access to Hundreds of Internal Tools
text.text: The Mercedes-Benz SSO platform uses a centralized LDAP system to manage user access authorization. After fuzzing a large number of websites, it was discovered that the vehicle maintenance internal tool access website umas.mercedes-benz.com had open user registration. The registration information was written to the same database as the core employee LDAP system. Using the registered information to access the SSO platform, successful login to git.mercedes-benz.com was achieved. Upon access, it was found that the internal GitHub contained source code and documentation for a large number of projects, such as Mercedes Me Connect, the application users employ to remotely control their vehicles. Internal documentation provided detailed explanations for developing remote control applications. While Mercedes-Benz requested further explanation of the impact, the security researcher discovered that using the registered information could obtain sensitive information, achieve remote code execution through exposed Spring Boot consoles (actuators) and dozens of sensitive internal applications used by employees. One of these applications was Mercedes-Benz Mattermost (Slack-based), which allowed joining any channel, including security channels, as well as impersonating internal employees to ask necessary questions to escalate privileges within the Mercedes-Benz network.

media.caption: Full Account Takeover on Ferrari and Arbitrary Account Creation allows Attacker to Access, Modify, and Delete All Customer Information and Access Administrative CMS Functionality to Manage Ferrari Websites

text.headline: Ferrari Full Account Takeover and Arbitrary Account Creation Allows Attacker to Access, Modify, Delete All Customer Information and Access Administrative CMS Functionality to Manage Ferrari Websites
text.text: After testing a large number of targets, researchers discovered that api.ferrari.com provides both user-facing and internal API interfaces for the Ferrari system. After analyzing the JavaScript code of a large number of dealer-related subdomains, they found that the dealer test website's single sign-on implementation had issues, with no restrictions on access to the underlying application. The apiKey for https://api.ferrari.com/cms/dws/back-office/ was exposed in the JS code. Using this API, one could access /cms/dws/back-office/auth/bo-users to retrieve all registered users, and also send POST requests to add a super admin user for themselves. Accessing /cms/dws/back-office/rest-connector-models returned a list of APIs and plaintext authentication headers. Using this information, users' personal information could be accessed, such as http://fcd.services.ferrari.com/core/api/v1/Users?email=ian@ian.sh. Sending a POST request to /core/api/v1/Users/:id/Roles could modify user roles, setting oneself as a super user or a Ferrari owner. Additionally, the returned information could be used to register new rest connectors and modify existing ones.

media.caption: SQL Injection and Regex Authorization Bypass on Spireon Systems allows Attacker to Access, Track, and Send Arbitrary Commands to 15 million Telematics systems and Additionally Fully Takeover Fleet Management Systems for Police Departments, Ambulance Services, Truckers, and Many Business Fleet Systems

text.headline: Spireon Systems SQL Injection and Regex Authentication Bypass Allows Attacker to Access, Track, and Send Arbitrary Commands to 15 Million Telematics Systems
text.text:
Spireon, a vehicle telematics company, offers aftermarket GPS trackers that can track and manage vehicles and receive arbitrary commands, such as locking the starter to prevent the vehicle from starting. Spireon systems have SQL injection and regex authentication bypass vulnerabilities, allowing attackers to access, track, and send arbitrary commands to 15 million devices.

SQL injection to bypass login:
The backend system admin.spireon.com login page has a SQL injection vulnerability. Using SQL injection payloads admin' # or administrator' # to log in results in a 301 redirect to the /dashboard page. Administrators can access all Spireon devices, obtain real-time positioning, send arbitrary commands to them, and also modify configurations, implant backdoors, and execute arbitrary commands through firmware updates. These devices are widely used in tractors, golf carts, police cars, and ambulances. Some can only obtain real-time positioning, while others can disable starters.

Using regex to bypass authentication
Testing revealed that URLs (such as /anything-admin-anything) containing "admin" and "dashboard" return 403 Forbidden, while URLs (such as /anything-anything) without these return 404 Not Found. Through enumerating %00-%FF, it was discovered that GET /%0dadmin and GET /%0ddashboard return 200 OK. Adding %0d to the front of the URL path bypassed authentication, allowing direct access to the backend.

media.caption: Mass Assignment on Reviver allows an Attacker to Remotely Track and Overwrite the Virtual License Plates for All Reviver Customers, Track and Administrate Reviver Fleets, and Access, Modify, and Delete All User Information

text.headline: Mass Assignment on Reviver Allows Attacker to Remotely Track and Overwrite Virtual License Plates for All Reviver Customers, Track and Administrate Reviver Fleets, and Access, Modify, and Delete All User Information
text.text:
In October 2022, California legalized electronic license plates. Most electronic license plates are issued by a company named Reviver. To obtain an electronic license plate, customers need to purchase Reviver's virtual electronic license plates. The virtual electronic license plates use SIM cards to support remote tracking and updates. Users of Reviver virtual license plates can update the plate's slogan, background, and mark the device as STOLEN after theft.

All APIs are on pr-api.rplate.com. Newly created users have their identity indicated by the "type" field in JSON, currently set to CONSUMER. A large amount of API information was found in the JS on the password reset page, including user roles. Modifying the "role" parameter to CORPORATE and refreshing achieved privilege escalation. After inviting a new account to register and logging in, not only did no authentication error occur, but fleet management functions could also be accessed. Fuzzing the "type" field with a dictionary revealed an anomaly: REVIVER_ROLE was changed to the number 4. Iterating from 0 to 100, it was found that 0 represents the role REVIVER. After setting this attribute and re-inviting a new user, although login was normal, the UI displayed abnormally and no buttons could be clicked. The researchers speculated that this was because although the user's privileges had been escalated, the user was accessing the frontend website rather than the backend page, causing errors that prevented operation. Using the current super admin user to directly call the API, they successfully obtained other users' information, viewed vehicle positioning, updated electronic license plates, deleted electronic license plates, and added new users.

text.headline: CHIMAERA: Hyundai, Kia, Genesis Infotainment Gen5W_L Series Firmware Update Signature Bypass
text.text:
The infotainment system update package signing for Hyundai Group brands (Hyundai, Kia, Genesis) has flaws that allow users to install custom firmware, such as implanting backdoors or injecting CAN messages. This research builds upon the team's previous research on Gen5 firmware (CVE-2020-8539 KOFFEE).
· CVE-2023-26243: The firmware decryption binary has an information leak during the firmware decryption process, allowing attackers to extract AES keys and initialization vectors from memory. Attackers can exploit this vulnerability to create custom firmware and implant backdoors in the infotainment system.
· CVE-2023-26244: During the firmware installation process, the firmware installer AppDMClient can be modified by attackers, thereby bypassing digital signature verification for the files AppUpgrade and .lge.upgrade.xml.
· CVE-2023-26245: The AppUpgrade program can be tampered with, allowing attackers to bypass firmware version checks and flash new or old versions, or even custom firmware.
· CVE-2023-26245: The AppUpgrade program can be tampered with, allowing attackers to bypass firmware signature checks, which indirectly permits attackers to install custom firmware.

All infotainment systems using Gen5W_L series firmware are affected. Tested versions include AE_E_PE_EUR.S5W_L001.001.211214 and 5W.XXX.S5W_L.001.001.221129. The researchers named this series of vulnerabilities CHIMAERA (Custom Hyundai Motor group infotAinmEnt fiRmwAre).

text.headline: Nissan North America Data Breach Caused by Third-Party Vendor Misconfiguration
text.text:
Nissan Motor North America officially sent data breach notifications to customers, informing them that a data breach incident caused by a third-party service vendor in 2022 affected approximately 17,998 customers. The leaked customer information included full names, dates of birth, and Nissan Financial account information, but did not include social media accounts or credit card information.

The notification disclosed that, upon investigation, data embedded in code during software testing was inadvertently and temporarily stored in a public cloud repository. Nissan stated that to date there was no evidence that the exposed information had been misused, and that customers were being notified out of an abundance of caution.

media.caption: Kia, Hyundai sued after viral TikTok causes rise in thefts

text.headline: Seattle Sues Hyundai, Kia Over Surge in Thefts (Anti-Theft Technology Not Adopted)
text.text:
The lawsuit alleges that other automakers universally adopt vehicle anti-theft technology to ensure that vehicles can only be started when a key is nearby. However, a large number of Hyundai and Kia vehicles in the United States still do not use anti-theft technology. As a result, Hyundai and Kia vehicles are more susceptible to theft than other vehicles. Models in Europe and Canada are not affected because regulations require anti-theft modules. Previously, Orange County, California had also filed a lawsuit.

The theft video #KiaBoyz went viral on video platforms like TikTok. Thieves only needed to remove the plastic shell on the steering column, expose the ignition switch, insert a USB plug into the key switch, and turn it several times to start the engine. The entire process took only a few minutes or even seconds. According to statistics, Hyundai and Kia theft incidents in July 2022 increased by 620% compared to the same period in 2021.

This also triggered a series of social safety issues. For example, some thrill-seeking young people copied the behavior, leading to dangerous driving after car theft, evading police pursuit, and crashes. In Buffalo, New York, a fatal accident occurred: 6 teenagers stole a Kia vehicle on October 23, 2020, and by the next morning, a crash occurred. All 5 passengers were ejected from the vehicle; 4 died and one 14-year-old girl was injured, while the 16-year-old male driver survived. The "Kia Boyz car theft challenge" was suspected to be the cause.

Affected models: Hyundai Elantra, Hyundai Kona, Hyundai Palisade, Hyundai Santa Cruz, Hyundai Santa Fe, Hyundai Sonata, Hyundai Tucson, Hyundai Venue, Kia Cadenza, Kia Forte, Kia K900, Kia Niro, Kia Optima, Kia Rio, Kia Sedona, Kia Seltos, Kia Sorrento, Kia Soul, Kia Sportage, Kia Stinger, and Kia Telluride

In response to this incident, the Hyundai Motor Group recalled nearly 4 million vehicles and established the website https://www.hyundaiantitheft.com for checking whether a vehicle is affected and for scheduling anti-theft software update appointments.

media.caption: How Mishandling of WebSockets Can Cause DoS and Energy Theft

text.headline: Charging Station Management System OCPP Protocol Session Management Implementation Flaw Can Cause Denial of Service or Free Charging
text.text:
OCPP (Open Charge Point Protocol) is a globally open communication standard aimed at enabling interoperability between charging stations and charging management systems. OCPP supports communication using HTTPS and WebSocket. In OCPP 1.6, authentication credentials are optional, with three authentication methods: ID only, ID and authentication credentials, and ID and client certificate. In the latest version 2.0.1, authentication credentials are mandatory.

The SaiFlow research team discovered a vulnerability in OCPP 1.6 WebSocket that can remotely cause charging station denial of service or free charging. Whether DoS or free charging occurs depends on the charging station's local configuration, including whether it supports offline authentication and charging, and whether AllowOfflineTxForUnknownId permits charging unknown vehicles after going offline. The research found that in WebSocket communication, the ID (CP3211) in the URL (ws://csms.provider.com:8080/webServices/ocpp/CP3211) is used as the unique identifier for the charging station. An attacker using the same ID to initiate a connection request to the charging management system will affect the normal session connection. Different charging management system implementations respond differently due to coding variations. Using the same ID to initiate a new connection has four possible outcomes:
1. The original connection is disconnected, the charging station loses network connectivity, and charging is denied (DoS). It will reconnect after a period of time.
2. The original connection remains alive but cannot receive response data from the server. The charging station's connection still exists, and no new connection is established. The attacker can only receive sensitive data from the charging management system through the created connection.
3. The original connection remains alive but cannot receive response data from the server. The new connection can receive the response data from the original connection's requests.
4. Both connections are normal, and both can receive response data for requests.

media.caption: Hacking into Toyota’s global supplier management network

text.headline: Toyota Global Supplier Information Management System Authentication Mechanism Vulnerability Allows Access to Large Amount of Data
text.text:
Toyota's web application Global Supplier Preparation Information Management System (GSPIMS) is used for project collaboration, research, procurement, and other supply chain management-related tasks between Toyota and its suppliers. GSPIMS is an Angular single-page application built on AG Grid.

Security researcher Eaton, during a 7-day penetration test of Toyota's cloud platform, discovered 4 critical vulnerabilities. One of the most severe was a backdoor login mechanism that required only knowing a user's email address to log into the system, including admin users. After analyzing the JS code and patching the CanActivate and CanActivateChild functions, Eaton could access backend pages but could not retrieve data. Further analysis revealed that the authentication Token JWT (JSON Web Token) was generated based solely on the email address, without requiring a password. Based on Toyota North America's email structure firstname.lastname@toyota.com, valid usernames could be guessed or valid email addresses could be collected from the internet. Sending a POST request to https://prd.svcs.gspims.toyota.com/qspims-1.0.0/custom/user/createJWT with a valid email address would return the jwtToken. Finally, assigning the jwtToken value to the cookie gspimsAccessToken would grant access to GSPIMS, including viewing and modifying 14K user accounts, sensitive files, projects, supplier rankings, supplier notes, and more.

The vulnerabilities were reported to Toyota in October 2022. Toyota completed remediation before disclosure — changing the HTTP response status for createJWT and findByEmail requests to 400 (Bad Request).

text.headline: Researchers Discovered Malformed Audio Files Crash Volkswagen Jetta and Chevrolet Equinox Media Players via Fuzzing
text.text:
A malformed ogg file on a USB drive caused the Volkswagen Jetta infotainment audio player to crash. Security researcher Jangeuntae performed fuzzing on the audio decoder of the Korean-market Volkswagen Jetta 2021 infotainment system and found that mutated ogg files on a USB drive could crash the player. Jangeuntae stated that the crash might be triggered by memory-related issues, and further analysis of the cause could potentially lead to more severe problems, such as remote code execution. The Volkswagen infotainment system has an auto-play feature when a USB drive is inserted. Exploiting this feature, Jangeuntae connected a computer to the infotainment system's USB port and continuously generated mutated, malformed multimedia files in WAV, MP3, WMA, and OGG formats. Approximately 20,000 mutated multimedia files were generated per day. After running the fuzzing program for one day, the defect was discovered — loading a particular ogg file caused the player to crash.

This defect was reported to Volkswagen prior to disclosure. Volkswagen officially stated that after assessment by their security incident response team, the issue was confirmed and classified as a product quality issue, with product improvements under consideration. Volkswagen expressed gratitude for Jangeuntae's research and looked forward to his next research project.

Additionally, the 2021 Chevrolet Equinox audio decoder also had a denial of service vulnerability. Jangeuntae designed a bit-flip fuzzer that generated a malformed mp3 audio file causing the player to crash. This defect was reported to General Motors and received acknowledgment.

media.caption: CONFIRMED

text.headline: Tesla Compromised Twice at Pwn2Own
text.text:
At the Pwn2Own competition held in Vancouver, Synacktiv security researchers demonstrated two independent vulnerabilities targeting the Tesla Model 3.

1. Exploiting a TOCTTOU (time-of-check-to-time-of-use) vulnerability in the gateway battery management system allowed opening the trunk while the vehicle was running. For this, they received $1 million in cash, 10 Master of Pwn points, and a brand-new Model 3.

2. Exploiting a heap overflow vulnerability and an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the Bluetooth chipset module, they breached Tesla's infotainment system. They moved from the Bluetooth chip to the host LINUX system, fully controlling the infotainment system, and demonstrated tampering with the boot animation and stealing data. This vulnerability earned the researchers $250,000 and the first-ever Tier 2 bounty designed for vulnerabilities of special significance.

media.caption: CAN Injection: keyless car theft

text.headline: CVE-2023-29389: In-the-Wild CAN Injection Theft of Toyota RAV4 2021 Discovered
text.text:
It was discovered in the wild that car thieves were using CAN injection to steal Toyota RAV4 2021 vehicles. By removing the bumper near the headlight to access the CAN bus, they send specific CAN messages (Key validated, unlock immobilizer) to deceive the vehicle into thinking the key is valid. The digital key ECU and the headlight ECU are on the same CAN network, which allows thieves to access the CAN network where the digital key ECU resides by removing the bumper. Due to the broadcast nature of the CAN bus, forged messages sent on the headlight wiring harness appear as if they originated from the digital key. The key-validated message is forwarded through the gateway to the engine control ECU on the powertrain CAN, which upon receipt disables the immobilizer. Similarly, messages to unlock doors can also be sent.

Security researcher Ian Tabor initially noticed his Toyota RAV4 2021 bumper was abnormal, having been removed multiple times within three months, before the vehicle was ultimately stolen. Tracking on the dark web and YouTube revealed that thieves were using emergency start devices costing up to €5000. The device's website offers over a hundred products ranging from matching fake keys to emergency start devices, purportedly intended for vehicle owners who lost their keys and reputable locksmiths. The targeted vehicle models include Jeep, Maserati, Honda, Renault, Jaguar, Fiat, Peugeot, Nissan, Ford, BMW, Volkswagen, Chrysler, Cadillac, GMC, and Toyota. The device used in this theft also supports Lexus ES, LC/LS/NX/RX, and Toyota GR Supra/Prius/Highlander/Land Cruiser/RAV4 models.

text.headline: Hyundai Discloses Personal Data Breach in France and Italy
text.text:
Hyundai sent data breach notification emails to vehicle owners in France and Italy. The leaked data included email addresses, physical addresses, phone numbers, chassis numbers, and other personal data, but did not include financial data.

media.caption: Apology and Report Regarding the Customer Information Leakage Incident Caused by Cloud Environment Misconfiguration and Measures to Prevent Recurrence

text.headline: Toyota Leaks Sensitive Data of 2.13 Million Vehicles: Real-Time Location Exposed for Nearly 10 Years
text.text:
On the 12th, Japanese automaker Toyota admitted that due to a misconfiguration in its cloud platform system, its Japan vehicle owner database had been "wide open" for nearly 10 years, putting the vehicle data of approximately 2.15 million Japanese users at risk of exposure.

This incident exposed customer information for those using Toyota T-Connect G-Link, G-Link Lite, and G-BOOK services between January 2, 2012, and April 17, 2023. Due to human error, the Toyota cloud platform system's account setting was configured as "public" instead of "private," leaving vehicle location data, identification numbers, and other data in an open state. The scope of impact was limited to vehicles within Japan, affecting approximately 2.15 million users who had registered for Toyota connected vehicle services, remote telematics services, and similar offerings, including some Lexus owners (a Toyota brand). The exposed detailed information did not include personally identifiable information, so unless an attacker knew the target vehicle's VIN (Vehicle Identification Number), they could not use this data to track a specific individual. A second statement published by Toyota on the "Toyota Connected" website also mentioned the possibility that video recordings taken outside the vehicle were exposed in this incident.

A spokesperson stated there was no evidence that the data had been leaked, copied, or maliciously used. Toyota had changed the settings and patched the system, and users could continue using cloud services as normal without needing to return to a dealership. Toyota committed to sending individual apology notifications to affected customers and established a dedicated call center to handle inquiries and requests from these vehicle owners.

media.caption: ASRG-China Community Discovers Critical T-Box Vulnerabilities in Sany Heavy Industry and Other Companies

text.headline: Sany Heavy Industry TBOX MQTT Insufficient Authentication Allows Tampering with Fleet Control and Status Data
text.text:
In November 2022, ASRG received vulnerability research reports from community security researchers. These vulnerabilities pose a serious security threat to vehicles from Sany Heavy Industry Co., Ltd and other OEMs using the same model TBox produced by Hangzhou Hopechart IoT Technology Co Ltd.

The Hopechart HQT-401 TBox has a vulnerability that leads to the leakage of the MQTT server address. Additionally, the insufficient authentication of the MQTT backend server for Sany Heavy Industry vehicles equipped with the Hopechart HQT-401 TBox allows attackers to access and even tamper with the control data and status data of the entire fleet. Multiple vulnerabilities include:
1. The MQTT backend does not require authentication, allowing attackers to make unauthorized connections.
2. Vehicles publish their telemetry data (e.g., GPS location, speed, odometer, fuel, etc.) as messages in public topics. The backend also sends commands to vehicles by publishing to public topics via MQTT. Therefore, attackers can access this sensitive and confidential data for the entire fleet managed by the backend.
3. MQTT messages sent by vehicles or the backend are neither encrypted nor authenticated. Attackers can create and publish messages to impersonate vehicles or the backend. For example, an attacker could send false information about a vehicle's location to deceive the backend.
4. The backend can inject data into a vehicle's Controller Area Network (CAN) bus by sending specific MQTT messages on public topics. Since these messages are neither authenticated nor encrypted, attackers can impersonate the backend, create fake messages, and inject control data into the CAN bus of any vehicle managed by the backend.

media.caption: JailBreakEC6:Feat(My First EV)!: Add Support for App Store

text.headline: NIO Infotainment System Misconfiguration and Directory Traversal Vulnerabilities Allow Privilege Escalation to Root
text.text:
Wen Guanxing, a security researcher from Pangu Lab, discovered that the NIO EC6 infotainment system Aspen versions below 3.2.5 have a misconfiguration in a system-privileged application (com.nextev.datastatistic). Exploiting this misconfiguration enabled privilege escalation from shell to system. Additionally, by exploiting a path traversal vulnerability in the Android prop property, privilege was escalated from system to Root. The vulnerability details were first disclosed at the MOSEC security conference in 2022.

· Privilege escalation from shell to system: In the AndroidManifest.xml configuration of the com.nextev.datastatistic application, android:debuggable = "true" and android:sharedUserId = "android.uid.system". By debugging the com.nextev.datastatistic application using the JDWP protocol, arbitrary code execution was achieved under system privileges (u:r:system_app:s0 context, uid = 1000).
· Privilege escalation from system to persistent root: Aspen does not enable kernel module signature verification by default. Privileged programs can load their own .ko files into the kernel via insmod. /system/bin/setup_touch.sh, platform_app, or system_app can setprop "persist.sys.touchscreen" to a value such as "cyttsp6_i2c.ko/../../../../data/system/exploit". The file /data/system/exploit.ko would then be inserted into the kernel, providing the attacker with persistent root privileges after reboot.

media.caption: Crashed EV Battery Packs Back on the Road with Cloned IDs? Shanghai Police Solve New Type of Computer Crime

text.headline: Illegal Tampering with NIO Vehicle Battery Pack Data, Faulty Battery Packs Back on the Road
text.text:
The Cybersecurity Division of the Jiading Branch of the Shanghai Municipal Public Security Bureau, while conducting work at the NIO vehicle manufacturer in their jurisdiction, discovered anomalies in the power battery data of some vehicles. Through the enterprise information system, officers found that within the same time period, battery packs with the same ID were simultaneously appearing and in use across multiple locations including Beijing, Jiangsu, Shanghai, and Fujian. After in-depth communication with the manufacturer's technical personnel, officers discovered that these vehicles with identical IDs had previously had their battery packs locked by the backend due to traffic accidents, rendering them unable to charge or drive. The data within these "cloned" battery packs with identical IDs had been illegally stolen and tampered with — specifically, the data from a healthy, intact battery pack was written into multiple faulty battery packs, thereby cracking the locking function.

According to national regulatory requirements (the "Interim Provisions on Traceability Management of New Energy Vehicle Power Battery Recycling" effective August 1, 2018), each power battery pack used in new energy vehicles has a unique battery ID number (24-character battery code). Faulty battery packs that are cloned and put back on the road pose an extremely high risk of battery short circuits or even fires, creating significant safety hazards.

The task force started from the battery backend database and, through meticulous analysis, discovered that three internet self-media accounts were using "battery unlocking" as a gimmick to publish instructional videos. Upon verification, these three self-media platforms corresponded to three auto repair businesses in other provinces and cities, and all involved vehicles were associated with these three businesses. This led to the identification of four criminal suspects, including Tu. The suspects Tu, Liu, and four others were apprehended, and chip writers, super programmers, and other tools used in the crimes were seized, promptly eliminating road safety hazards.

According to the suspects' confessions, since 2022, the criminal gang had used tools to read data from the battery packs of multiple normal, intact vehicles. They then purchased accident vehicles and faulty battery packs from various auction platforms and used car dealers, wrote the intact data into the faulty battery packs, completely overwriting the original data of the faulty battery packs, and created cloned battery packs identical to the original. This bypassed the backend locking function and allowed the faulty battery packs to be recharged and put back on the road. The criminal gang charged between 1,000 and 3,000 RMB per battery unlock, accumulating approximately 50,000 RMB in illegal profits.

media.caption: Jailbreaking an Electric Vehicle in 2023 or What It Means to Hotwire Tesla's x86-Based Seat Heater

text.headline: Jailbreaking Tesla Infotainment System via Fault Injection
text.text:
The AMD Secure Processor contains a fault injection vulnerability that allows bypassing secure boot, gaining root access to the Tesla infotainment system and sensitive information.

At BlackHat 2023, three PhD students from Technical University of Berlin — Christian Werling, Niclas Kühnapfel, Hans Niklas Jacob — along with security researcher Oleg Drokin, presented the process of breaking the secure boot of Tesla's AMD Zen 1 Secure Processor (ASP). They used voltage fault injection to bypass the firmware integrity verification of the secure boot, extracted the firmware to implant a backdoor, and flashed it back to obtain root access to the Tesla infotainment system. After gaining root access, they further researched the TPM (Trusted Platform Module) object sealing and unsealing process, ultimately retrieving system and user sensitive data from NVMe storage. They extracted a vehicle-unique, hardware-bound RSA key used for vehicle authentication and authorization in Tesla's internal service network, and were also able to decrypt encrypted user personal sensitive information such as contacts and calendars.

media.caption: FORD PROVIDES CUSTOMER GUIDANCE IN RESPONSE TO SUPPLIER DISCLOSURE OF CYBER SECURITY VULNERABILITY

text.headline: Ford Vulnerability Statement: Customer Guidance in Response to TI Supplier's Wi-Fi Vulnerability Disclosure
text.text:
Ford learned from its Wi-Fi module supplier Texas Instruments (TI) that the Wi-Fi driver used in the SYNC3 infotainment system contains a buffer overflow vulnerability affecting certain Ford and Lincoln vehicles. Supplier TI informed Ford of the Wi-Fi defect and immediately took action to validate, assess impact, and develop mitigation measures. Ford stated that a patch would be released soon, available for online download and installation via USB. Prior to the patch release, concerned customers can simply disable the Wi-Fi function through the SYNC 3 infotainment system's settings menu.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2023-29468, resides in the WL18xx MCP driver of the Wi-Fi subsystem integrated in the automotive infotainment system. The management frames do not restrict the data length of XCC_EXT_1_IE_I and XCC_EXT_2_IE_ID, allowing an attacker within Wi-Fi range to use a specially crafted oversized management frame to trigger a buffer overflow, potentially leading to remote code execution.

media.caption: It’s Official: Cars Are the Worst Product Category We Have Ever Reviewed for Privacy
media.credit: Cars | Privacy & security guide | Mozilla Foundation

text.headline: Mozilla Publishes Privacy Investigation Report on 25 Automotive Brands
text.text:
Mozilla's privacy investigation covering smart scenarios including vehicles, wearables, and smart home devices found that automotive privacy issues are the worst. Researchers found that major global automotive brands including Chevrolet, Nissan, Toyota, Kia, Audi, Jeep, Honda, and Volkswagen intrusively collected personal information through sensors, microphones, cameras, apps, and connected vehicle services. Typically without users' explicit consent, automotive companies began collecting personal information the moment people entered the vehicle.

Based on the investigation of 25 automotive brands:
1. Excessive data collection: Every automotive brand collected more data than necessary, including highly intimate information ranging from medical data, genetic data to sexual activity. General Motors' Cadillac, GMC, Buick, and Chevrolet stated in their California privacy notices that they could collect "genetic, physiological, behavioral, and biometric" data. Kia and Nissan also stated they could collect "genetic information." Nissan stated it could collect information about users' "sexual activity" and "intelligence" (inferred from personal data), and could share this information with "marketing and promotional partners" or for their own "direct marketing purposes."
2. 84% of automakers shared personal privacy data with service providers, automotive data centers, and other unknown entities for research, marketing, or other vague commercial purposes. 56% stated they could share data with requesting government and law enforcement agencies. 76% (19 brands) indicated they might sell personal data to third parties. Insurance companies could dynamically adjust premiums by analyzing driving habits, speed, and braking data.
3. 92% of vehicle owners could not control their own data. Only 2 out of 25 brands supported deleting personal information.
4. Rarely met regulatory requirements and failed to safeguard data properly. In the past three years, 86% of automotive brands experienced data breaches, hacker attacks, or privacy violations against vehicle owners.
5. 52% (13 brands) of automotive brands collected data outside the vehicle, including weather, road conditions, traffic signs, and other environmental information.

media.caption: Enabling ADB and Network ADB on XPeng P5 and XPeng G9

text.headline: XPeng P5/G9 Debug Entrance Publicly Disclosed
text.text:
Multiple posts titled "XPeng Friends United" were published on the official XPeng community, urging XPeng to push OTA updates for older models to match the infotainment experience of newer models. Subsequently, the method to enable ADB on XPeng P5 (OTA 3.5.0 and earlier), XPeng G9 (OTA 4.3.1 and earlier), XPeng G6 (untested), XPeng P7 (OTA 2.10 and earlier), or XPeng G3 was publicly released on GitHub. The engineering mode password uses a per-device unique key that can be calculated from the device ID.

1. Open the vehicle's dialer interface and enter *#9925*111#* to display a QR code on screen
2. Read the QR code to obtain the ID, in the format XPENGD55xxxxxxxxxxxxxx
3. Calculate the unlock code from XPENGD55xxxxxxxxxxxxxx (e.g., *#03*12345678*#)
4. Enter the unlock code in the vehicle's dialer interface. The unlock code will automatically disappear; if it does not, manually delete all content
5. Enter *#9387*141#* in the dialer interface to enter engineering mode
6. Enable USB ADB debugging and ADB network debugging in engineering mode.

text.headline: Mazda Official Website Defaced, Redirected to Adult Content Site

text.text:
Alpine Corporation (Japan), founded in 1967, is a specialized automotive electronics company primarily producing car audio and automotive communication systems, with over 30 overseas subsidiaries across more than 10 countries. It supplies over 40,000 types of components to more than 2,000 automotive companies worldwide.

On September 10, 2023, Alpine detected unauthorized access to its servers, immediately isolated the affected servers, and launched an investigation with security advisors. media.caption: Apology and Notification Regarding Possible Leakage of Personal Information Due to Unauthorized Access

text.headline: Mazda Issues Apology Announcement for Data Leak
text.text: On September 15, Mazda issued a statement indicating that on July 24, 2023, it detected unauthorized access to its servers by external attackers, potentially leading to the leakage of some personal information. However, Mazda emphasized that the compromised servers did not store any customer personal information, and therefore no such information was leaked. The company expressed deep regret for the inconvenience and concern this incident may have caused to affected individuals. The potentially leaked information consists of partial personal information managed by the company, including names and phone numbers of employees and partners, totaling approximately 104,732 records. Mazda stated that it had disabled the unauthorized access IDs, shut down the affected servers, and reported the incident to police and the Personal Information Protection Commission. The company will cooperate with relevant organizations to confirm the final impact and take appropriate measures with the assistance of external security experts. Mazda stated it would take the incident seriously and implement all possible measures, such as improving security systems for all websites and networks and enhancing monitoring systems to prevent similar incidents from recurring.

media.caption: A roadmap to $50,000 at Pwn2Own Vehicle 2024: Dissecting QNX and exploiting its vulnerabilities

text.headline: 360's Roadmap to Pwn2Own Automotive
text.text:
At the POC2023 security conference, two security researchers from 360 — Yingjie Cao and Zhe Jing — presented a talk titled "A roadmap to $50,000 at Pwn2Own Vehicle 2024: Dissecting QNX, and exploiting its vulnerabilities," providing a comprehensive analysis of QNX, delving into its architecture, design, and overall security posture. They shared a complete attack chain targeting infotainment systems using QNX. The two exploited vulnerabilities are as follows:

1. An integer overflow vulnerability in the BMP image parsing library libimg.so.1 caused a stack overflow during memcpy. By overwriting the return address with the address of system() in libc, arbitrary command execution was achieved.
2. A race condition vulnerability (double-fetch, sometimes manifesting as TOCTOU) in the kernel-to-user message passing function ker_msg_sendv. After successful exploitation, privilege escalation from normal user to root was achieved.

media.caption: Data Privacy Investigation: Chinese Electric Vehicle Exports

text.headline: TOP10VPN: Data Privacy Investigation Report on Chinese EV Exports
text.text:
With the large-scale export of Chinese electric vehicles, TOP10VPN investigated 10 brands including Aiways, BYD, Great Wall Motors, Human Horizons, MG, NIO, Polestar, Volvo, XPeng, and Zeekr, analyzing the data privacy risks of exported vehicles and mobile applications. The investigation report noted:

· Poor privacy policies: 7 manufacturers' policies did not meet standards, with one (Polestar) lacking an adequate policy altogether. Issues included lack of detail, improper translations, broken links, and casual statements.
· Mobile app data collection: All 10 brands collected location data, 7 collected IP addresses, 3 tracked app/vehicle browsing activity, 2 accessed app/vehicle message content; at least 3 collected unique IMEI identifiers.
· Vehicle-side data collection: 6 tracked vehicle location via GPS, 4 recorded driving trips, 3 monitored driver speed, 3 did not disclose data collection policies.
· Inaccurate app store privacy labels: 8 iOS apps and 6 Android apps had potentially misleading privacy labels.
· Android app permission risks: 8 apps had more than 10 risky permissions, 4 apps had more than 20 risky permissions, with Zeekr having 36 in particular.

media.caption: Toyota confirms breach after Medusa ransomware threatens to leak data

text.headline: Toyota Confirms Medusa Ransomware Attack
text.text:
Toyota Financial Services (TFS) confirmed an attack by the Medusa ransomware group, having detected unauthorized access to its systems in Europe and Africa. Toyota Financial Services is a subsidiary of Toyota Motor Corporation, operating globally with business coverage spanning 90% of Toyota Motor's markets, providing automotive financing services to Toyota customers.

The Medusa ransomware group added Toyota Financial Services to its dark web data leak site's victim list, demanding an $8 million ransom to delete the leaked data. Medusa gave Toyota 10 days to respond, with an option to extend the deadline at a cost of $10,000 per day in "late fees." To prove the attack, Medusa released sample data from Toyota Financial, including financial documents, spreadsheets, purchase invoices, hashed account passwords, plaintext user IDs and passwords, agreements, passport scans, internal organizational charts, financial performance reports, employee email addresses, and more. Medusa also provided a .TXT file containing the file tree structure of all data they claimed to have stolen from Toyota's systems. Most of these files were in German, indicating that the hackers had successfully accessed Toyota's Central European business systems.

In a statement to security media BleepingComputer, a Toyota spokesperson stated:
· Toyota Financial Services Europe and Africa recently detected unauthorized system activity at a limited number of locations.
· We shut down certain systems to investigate the activity and mitigate risk, and have begun cooperating with law enforcement.
· To date, this incident is limited to Toyota Financial Services Europe and Africa regions.
· Most countries have already initiated system recovery processes.

media.caption: Stellantis production affected by cyberattack at auto supplier

text.headline: Yanfeng International Hit by Cyberattack, Stellantis Production Affected
text.text:
Global automaker Stellantis stated on the 13th that a cyberattack on an automotive supplier had disrupted its operations, affecting production of Chrysler, Dodge, Jeep, and Ram models.

The cyberattack primarily affected Chinese supplier Yanfeng International Automotive Technology Co. Ltd. By the evening of the 13th, the company's website was inaccessible. Stellantis spokesperson Anne Marie Fortunate issued a statement: "Due to an issue with an external supplier, production at certain Stellantis assembly plants in North America has been disrupted. We are monitoring the situation and working with the supplier to mitigate further impact on our operations."

On November 27, the ransomware group Qilin claimed responsibility for the attack, posting multiple samples on the dark web as evidence of their access to Yanfeng's systems and files, including financial documents, non-disclosure agreements, quotation documents, technical data sheets, and internal reports.

media.caption: reach Notifications
media.credit: Auto parts giant AutoZone warns of MOVEit data breach

text.headline: Auto Parts Dealer AutoZone Discloses Data Breach
text.text:
AutoZone is one of the largest aftermarket auto parts retailers in the United States, operating 7,140 stores across the U.S., Mexico, Puerto Rico, Brazil, and the U.S. Virgin Islands. Following a cyberattack, AutoZone filed a data breach notification with the Maine Attorney General's Office on November 21, 2023, and immediately notified 184,995 affected users.

MOVEit is a file transfer application developed by Progress Software, which AutoZone used to store and transfer some sensitive data. Over 2,000 organizations globally were affected by the MOVEit file transfer application vulnerability. In late May 2023, the Cl0p ransomware group exploited a SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2023-34362) in the popular MOVEit file transfer solution to steal sensitive data from numerous organizations. Victims included many well-known companies, government agencies (e.g., multiple U.S. federal agencies and the U.S. Department of Energy), financial institutions, pension systems, and other public and private entities, including AutoZone. The Cl0p ransomware group stole a large amount of internal sensitive data from AutoZone's systems. The obtained data totaled approximately 1.1 GB, containing employee names, email addresses, parts supply details, tax information, payroll files, Oracle database files, store, production and sales information, users' Social Security numbers, and more.

After discovering the data breach, AutoZone temporarily disabled the MOVEit application, rebuilt affected systems, and patched the vulnerability. It simultaneously launched an investigation and engaged external cybersecurity experts for assistance. AutoZone also sent data breach notification letters to affected consumers, informing them of the leaked information and providing one year of free fraud detection and identity theft protection through Equifax. AutoZone advised consumers to regularly check their credit reports to prevent identity theft or other fraudulent activities, and to be cautious about clicking links or downloading attachments in suspicious emails.

media.caption: Vulnerabilities in Skoda and Volkswagen vehicles

text.headline: PCAutomotive Discloses Multiple Skoda Vulnerabilities
text.text:
Automotive security company PCAutomotive discovered multiple low-to-medium severity vulnerabilities distributed across both vehicle-side and cloud-side components during its research on the 2022 Skoda Superb III from the Volkswagen Group. These vulnerabilities could lead to the leakage of sensitive user information and provide potential attackers with unauthorized access to and operation of vehicle functions, including access to the MIB3 infotainment unit's debug interface, denial of service via the in-vehicle Wi-Fi network, and attacks exploiting the infotainment unit's UDS authentication (Security Access).

The vehicle is equipped with an MIB3 infotainment system manufactured by Preh (acquired by Ningbo Joyson Electronic in 2011), supporting smart connectivity features such as Android Auto, Apple CarPlay, and MirrorLink.

The following is a list of key issues and vulnerabilities:
· The SWD debug interface of the infotainment unit was not disabled, posing a potential access risk.
· The power control chip has a UART debug terminal, providing an additional attack surface.
· CVE-2023-28895: The UART debug interface of the power control chip uses hardcoded credentials, easily cracked by attackers.
· CVE-2023-28896: UDS service password uses weak encoding.
· CVE-2023-28897: UDS service contains hardcoded passwords.
· CVE-2023-28898: Apple CarPlay can cause denial of service in the infotainment system.
· CVE-2023-28899: Denial of service can be initiated via UDS ECU service.
· CVE-2023-28900: Cloud backend service leaks user nicknames, queryable by specifying a VIN.
· CVE-2023-28901: Server-side leaks trip data, queryable by specifying a VIN.

media.caption: IMPORTANT UPDATE FROM NISSAN OCEANIA

text.headline: Nissan Hit by Cyberattack in Australia and New Zealand
text.text:
On December 7, Nissan Oceania (Australia and New Zealand) posted an announcement on its website confirming a cyberattack, with financial services systems, some supplier systems, and after-sales service systems affected. The company was working to restore its systems as quickly as possible and would continue to publish incident updates via nissan.com.au and nissan.co.nz. Nissan was working with global incident response teams and other relevant stakeholders to investigate the scope of the incident and whether any personal information had been accessed. Nissan encouraged customers to remain vigilant about their accounts, including watching for any abnormal or fraudulent activity. Nissan had also notified the Australian Cyber Security Centre and New Zealand's National Cyber Security Centre. Nissan assured customers that credit rating issues arising from the financial services system outage would not be affected.

The ransomware group AKIRA claimed responsibility for the incident and publicly released 128 GB of data. The leaked data included employee information files, NDAs, project data, partner information, and customer information, including Nissan, Mitsubishi, Renault, Skyline, Infiniti, LDV, and RAM suppliers. Over 10% of personal government identification documents were leaked, including approximately 4,000 Medicare cards, 7,500 driver's licenses, 220 passports, and 1,300 tax file numbers. The remaining 90% of personal information was affected, including loan-related documents, employment details, and dates of birth.

To support affected customers, Nissan provided the following services: free access to IDCARE, free credit monitoring services through Equifax in Australia and Centrix in New Zealand, and reimbursement for replacement costs of stolen government identification documents.

media.caption: EasyPark Data Breach

text.headline: EasyPark Suffers Cyberattack, Leaking Millions of User Records
text.text:
EasyPark is a Swedish company whose mobile web application serves as a parking spot locator, reservation manager, and EV charging point finder. The company operates digital parking services across 20 countries and more than 4,000 cities, covering much of Europe, the United States, Australia, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom. The EasyPark app (European version) has surpassed 10 million downloads on Google Play, while the other apps RingGo (UK version) and ParkMobile (US version) have 5 million installations each.

Following the cyberattack, an EasyPark spokesperson declined to provide details about the incident or the number of affected customers, but acknowledged that some European users may be impacted. Information that users provided to the platform, such as names, phone numbers, physical addresses, and email addresses, was leaked. The company stated that the stolen data cannot be used for payments, that passwords of affected users were immediately reset following the incident, and that relevant authorities were notified.

media.caption: Dubai’s largest taxi app exposes 220K+ users

text.headline: Dubai Taxi Company Database Misconfiguration Exposes Massive Amount of Data
text.text:
The Cybernews research team discovered that the Dubai Taxi Corporation (DTC), a taxi business under the Dubai Roads and Transport Authority (RTA), had its application leaking a large volume of sensitive information, including personal data of over 197,000 users and nearly 23,000 drivers. The exposed data was stored in an open MongoDB database, which has since been secured. The DTC app has over 100,000 downloads on the Google Play Store. DTC stated that it holds a 44% market share in Dubai, operates over 7,000 vehicles, and has 14,000 active driver partners.

The research team believes the leaked database was likely a production database used for development purposes, as it contained customer data, logs, driver personally identifiable information, registration and bank details, and passenger order details. The data spans from 2018 to 2021. Exposed user data included email addresses, phone numbers, phone models, and app tokens (used for registration, login, and sessions). Using the exposed tokens, unauthorized access to any account was possible.

The research team attempted to contact DTC, but as of the article's publication, had received no response from DTC.

media.caption: Porsche Macan canned: European sales to stop in 2024

text.headline: Porsche ICE Macan Fails to Meet WP.29 Cybersecurity Regulation Requirements, to Cease European Sales
text.text:
Porsche stated that when the current Macan model was designed and developed, the UNECE (United Nations Economic Commission for Europe) cybersecurity regulations WP.29 R155/R156 had not yet been introduced. Since the vehicle is already at the end of its product lifecycle, the cost of updating it to comply with the new regulations would be prohibitively high. Additionally, a vehicle that does not comply with UNECE WP.29 regulations faces fines of up to 30,000 euros. As a result, the company had no choice but to discontinue this popular SUV model. This means the ICE Porsche Macan is the first vehicle model to be discontinued due to cybersecurity regulatory requirements.

Under UNECE WP.29 regulations, all new vehicles sold in the EU must comply with provisions related to "advanced driver assistance systems, automated driving systems, and cybersecurity." The R155 regulation mandates that from July 1, 2022, newly introduced vehicle models must obtain cybersecurity system type approval (VTA); from July 1, 2024, all models still in production must also obtain cybersecurity system type approval to be sold in the EU, UK, Japan, and South Korean markets.

The Macan has been a very important model for Porsche in Europe, with over 20,000 units sold in 2023. This popular SUV will be withdrawn from the EU market in April 2024, while other global regions are unaffected for now. The new all-electric Macan, developed on the PPE platform, will be launched in 2024 to replace the ICE version. Additionally, it remains unclear whether the Audi Q5, which shares the same MLB platform as the Macan, is affected by the WP.29 cybersecurity regulation.
